title: International IPR — Paris, Berne, PCT, Madrid System and TRIPS Enforcement

content.overview: Paris, Berne, the PCT, the Madrid Protocol and TRIPS are the main international instruments. Paris covers industrial property priority. Berne covers copyright national treatment. PCT delays national patent filings. Madrid is a trade-mark filing system. TRIPS sets enforcement minima. An international filing is not a granted Indian right. National prosecution still decides grant.
content.glance: International IPR — Paris, Berne, PCT, Madrid System and TRIPS Enforcement. Complete IPR treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Paris gives priority, not a grant.

cases.name: R.G. Anand v. Deluxe Films
cases.facts: The dispute concerned alleged copying of a dramatic work into a film.
cases.issue: What test determines substantial copyright infringement of an idea or expression.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Copyright protects expression, not ideas, and infringement depends on substantial similarity assessed from the work as a whole.
cases.holding: The Court stated the governing comparison test.
cases.relevance: Use for copyright infringement and idea-expression distinction.

cases.name: Novartis AG v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court considered patentability of a pharmaceutical form under s. 3(d).
cases.issue: What enhanced efficacy threshold applies to a pharmaceutical derivative.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 3(d) requires the statutory enhanced-efficacy threshold and prevents evergreening without the required proof.
cases.holding: The patent claim was rejected under the statutory standard.
cases.relevance: Use for patentability exclusions and pharmaceutical patents.

cases.name: Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals Ltd.
cases.facts: The parties used similar marks for pharmaceutical products.
cases.issue: How should deceptive similarity be assessed in pharmaceutical trademark disputes.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts must apply a stricter likelihood-of-confusion test for medicines because confusion may endanger public health.
cases.holding: The Court directed a careful comparison of the marks and circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for trademark confusion and public-interest analysis.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: An international filing is not a granted Indian right. National prosecution still decides grant.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Paris Convention; Berne Convention; Patent Cooperation Treaty; Madrid Protocol; TRIPS.
essentialIngredients: No international registration treated as Indian grant
enhancement.detailedExplanation: A Paris priority date can be claimed in India within the enacted period. Berne means India protects foreign works without a formality the Convention forbids. A PCT application must still enter the Indian national phase. A Madrid international registration is examined under the Trade Marks Act. TRIPS enforcement is implemented by the Indian remedies, not by a direct suit on the treaty.
enhancement.examples: A foreign patent applicant claims a 12-month priority. The Indian application is still examined under the Patents Act. A Madrid request is refused if the Indian absolute grounds fail.
